name: STM8L101F3P6TR
title: STM8L101x1/x2/x3 8-bit ultra-low-power microcontrollers, up to 8 Kbytes Flash, timers, comparators, USART, SPI, I2C
summary: STM8L101x1/x2/x3 are 8-bit ultra-low-power microcontrollers with an STM8 core at up to 16 MHz, 2 to 8 Kbytes of Flash (up to 2 Kbytes usable as data EEPROM on the 8-Kbyte parts) and 1.5 Kbytes of RAM, running from 1.65 V to 3.6 V. They carry two 16-bit timers, an 8-bit timer, two comparators, USART, SPI, I2C, an infrared output, beeper, independent watchdog and auto-wakeup, all clocked from internal 16 MHz and 38 kHz RC oscillators. Halt draws 0.3 µA and Active-halt 0.8 µA typical. Packages are TSSOP20, UFQFPN20, UFQFPN28, UFQFPN32 and LQFP32; STM8L101F3P6TR is the 8-Kbyte TSSOP20 part for -40 °C to 85 °C on tape and reel.
key_figures: 2, 4 or 8 Kbytes (8-Kbyte parts: up to 2 Kbytes data EEPROM)
150 µA/MHz + 215 µA (estimate); 2.70 mA typ at 16 MHz from Flash
16 MHz HSI (±1 % at 25 °C, 3 V), 38 kHz LSI
up to 30, 18 on 20-pin packages; 20 mA high sink/source

tables.title: Pin description (pin numbers, I/O capability, functions)
rows: USART synchronous clock / Configurable clock output
SWIM input and output / Beep output / Timer Infrared output
notes: Type: I input, O output, S supply. HS: 20 mA high sink/source. wpu: weak pull-up. Output column codes: OD open-drain, PP push-pull, T a true open-drain pin.
"(reset)" marks the configuration the pin takes once internal reset is released; unless a note says otherwise it is the same while reset is held.
(1) On parts with a COMP_REF pin every port of the 32-pin package is active; all of them are to be configured as inputs with pull-up.
(2) After power-up NRST/PA1 is a reset input with pull-up. Reconfigured as PA1 it works only as a push-pull output, never as open-drain output or general-purpose input.
(3) PB0 and PB4 carry a pull-up while reset is held and become floating inputs after release.
(4) A true open-drain I/O has no P-channel buffer, no weak pull-up and no protection diode to VDD.
(5) PA0 is an input with pull-up both during reset and after release.
(6) PA0 has the high-sink LED driver capability.
Output slope control is programmable on every GPIO except the true open-drain pins; it defaults to a 2 MHz limit.

circuits.title: Recommended NRST pin configuration
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, with an optional external reset source on the same node. The internal pull-up RPU charges the capacitor; the capacitor filters spurious resets. The external source must be able to pull NRST below VIL(NRST) max.

parts.note: 10 nF minimum; smaller values cut charge current

notes: When NRST also resets other devices, the capacitor's charge and discharge time sets the reset pulse those devices see.
An external reset circuit is recommended for a correct reset on power-down while VPDR < VDD < VDD min.

operation.text: STM8L101x1, x2 and x3 are the low-density members of the STM8L low-power 8-bit line, with 2, 4 or 8 Kbytes of Flash, 1.5 Kbytes of RAM and the same pinout and memory map across the family. Only the 8-Kbyte parts hold data EEPROM, up to 2 Kbytes carved out of the Flash. Register-level detail is in reference manual RM0013 and programming detail in PM0054.
The 8-bit STM8 CISC core reaches 16 MIPS at 16 MHz, addresses a 24-bit linear space, and has 21 internal registers, 20 addressing modes and 80 instructions.

A single-wire interface (SWIM, on PA0) reaches the debug module and memories in every operating mode, for in-circuit debugging without halting the application and for fast Flash programming. CPU state is visible in real time through shadow registers.

Nested interrupt controller with three software priority levels and 26 vectors of fixed hardware priority. Up to 29 external interrupt sources map onto 10 vectors; every I/O can be routed to an external interrupt. Trap and reset are separate vectors.

Program Flash and data EEPROM can be write-protected separately through the memory access security mechanism (MASS). One 64-byte block holds option bytes, 5 of them used by the device. The non-volatile memory has error correction (ECC). In-application and in-circuit programming are both supported, with read-out protection selectable.

Wait: the CPU clock stops while selected peripherals run at full speed. Active-halt: CPU and peripheral clocks stop and the auto-wakeup unit ends the mode after a programmed time. Halt: all clocks stop, power and RAM contents stay, and an external interrupt wakes the part. Typical figures are 0.3 µA in Halt, 0.8 µA in Active-halt and 150 µA/MHz running.
An internal regulator makes the 1.8 V core and peripheral supply. It has a main mode and a low-power mode; entering Halt or Active-halt switches it to the low-power mode on its own to save current.

The system clock comes from the 16 MHz internal RC oscillator (HSI) through a programmable prescaler; HSI wakeup is typically 4 µs. A 38 kHz low-speed internal RC (LSI) clocks the independent watchdog and the auto-wakeup unit. The clock controller gates peripheral clocks for low-power operation, and PC4 can output a configurable clock (CCO).
Runs from the LSI, so it keeps working if the CPU clock fails. Option byte OPT4 selects whether hardware or software starts it and whether it stops in Halt and Active-halt.

TIM2 and TIM3 are 16-bit up/down auto-reload timers with a programmable prescaler and two channels each, for time bases, input capture, output compare, PWM and one-pulse mode, with interrupts on capture, compare, overflow, break and trigger. TIM4 is an 8-bit up-counting auto-reload timer with a 7-bit prescaler, for a time base with an overflow interrupt. The auto-wakeup counter ends Active-halt.

The beeper produces 1, 2 or 4 kHz when the LSI runs at 38 kHz. The infrared interface combines two timer output-compare channels into a remote-control waveform on IR_TIM (PA0), the pin with the high-sink LED driver (80 mA absolute maximum sink current); the driver is set up in the IR_CR register.

COMP1 and COMP2 are zero-crossing comparators sharing one bias and one reference. The reference is either ground (internal) or the COMP_REF pin. Each comparator selects among 4 input channels, its output polarity can be inverted, and it can raise an interrupt, a timer input capture or a timer break.

The standard UFQFPN20 and UFQFPN28 parts have no COMP_REF pin; the A-suffix versions (STM8L101F1U6ATR, F2U6ATR, F3U6ATR, G2U6ATR, G3U6ATR) bring it out on PA6, in place of PA3 on UFQFPN20 and of PA5 on UFQFPN28. UFQFPN32 and LQFP32 share one pinout.

On the A-suffix parts every port of the 32-pin die is live even where it has no pin. Configure all of them as inputs with pull-up to avoid spurious behaviour; until that is done, during power-up and reset, supply current can rise slightly, typically under 300 µA.

USART: full-duplex asynchronous NRZ with a fractional baud-rate generator, plus a synchronous clock output. SPI: full or half duplex, master or slave, multi-master capable, up to 8 MHz. I2C: multi-master and slave, standard and fast mode up to 400 kHz, with arbitration and bus sequencing in hardware; a matching address wakes the part from Halt or Active-halt.

Up to 30 I/Os (18 on 20-pin packages). Each can be a floating or pulled-up input, with or without interrupt, or an open-drain or push-pull output. All except PC0 and PC1 are high sink/source (20 mA class) with a 45 kΩ typical weak pull-up. PC0 and PC1 are true open-drain: no driver to VDD, no pull-up and no clamp to VDD, so they accept up to VDD + 4.0 V but no positive injection. PA0 adds the high-sink LED driver. Output slew is programmable, 2 MHz by default.

An ultra-low-power power-on/power-down reset holds the part in reset below VPOR at power-up (1.35 V to 1.65 V) and below VPDR on power-down (1.40 V to 1.60 V); release follows about 1 ms after VDD rises. The VDD rise rate is specified from 20 µs/V to 1300 µs/V, and power-on reset is guaranteed while the 1300 µs/V limit is met. NRST is a CMOS input with a permanent pull-up; pulses under 50 ns are filtered and pulses over 300 ns are taken. Reconfigured as PA1 the pin becomes a push-pull output only.

A capacitor from NRST to ground guards against parasitic resets; 10 nF is the smallest recommended value, and a smaller one lowers the charge current in power-sensitive designs. Whatever drives NRST must take it below VIL(NRST) max, or the reset is not seen internally.

OPT1 sets read-out protection (0xAA enables it), OPT2 the size of the write-protected user boot code area in pages, OPT3 the number of 64-byte data EEPROM pages at the top of the 8-Kbyte Flash, and OPT4 the watchdog start and Halt behaviour. Address 0x4807 must hold 0x00. Option bytes are written only over SWIM in ICP mode.

A 96-bit factory identifier at 0x4925 to 0x4930, read a byte at a time, encodes wafer X and Y position, wafer number and lot number. It cannot be changed, and can serve as a serial number, as input to code-security schemes, or for secure boot.

All voltages are relative to VSS. Min and max limits hold over the full temperature, supply and frequency range and are production-tested at 25 °C and at the top of the selected temperature range, except where a note marks them as characterization, design or simulation values (mean ± 3 sigma). Limits above 85 °C apply to suffix 3 parts only. Typical values are at 25 °C and VDD = 3 V and are not tested; typical curves are design guidance.

Unexpected resets and program-counter corruption can usually be reproduced by forcing NRST low for 1 second; ESD applied directly to the device can be used to find weaknesses, and the firmware hardened against them (application note AN1015).
Keep switching I/Os, negative injection and fast edges away from the comparator inputs and from unused comparator inputs; large series resistors on the inputs make these effects worse.
UFQFPN32 has an exposed die pad on its underside; solder it to PCB ground. Solder every lead and pad of the UFQFPN package to the board for solder-joint life.
